Case study · Technical

Smart Systems Research Laboratory

Mechanical Engineering & Technical Systems Intern (SWEP II) · September 2025 to October 2025. I designed and modelled a 4-degree-of-freedom robot arm in SolidWorks and presented the project in October 2025.

Documentation and communication work

Alongside designing the arm in SolidWorks, my internship work on a multi-joint robotic arm system supported fabrication teams and research supervisors.

  • Technical documentation of the arm system
  • 2D production drawings and visual assembly schematics
  • Motion simulation and structural stress evaluation
  • Reporting progress and engineering trade-offs to senior supervisors

The arm

Robot arm

A mechanical device designed to work like a human arm. It can pick, place and assemble objects.

How I thought it through

Learn the building blocks

Started with four SolidWorks features: extrude base, cut extrude, linear pattern, and rib and chamfer.

Break the arm into parts

Split the arm into a base that supports it, links that connect the joints, and a gripper that works at the end.

Model each part

Built the base, the links and the gripper as separate parts before joining them.

Define the motion

Gave the arm 4 degrees of freedom, with joints that let the links rotate or bend.

Assemble and test

Put the parts together in an assembly and recorded myself moving the arm to check how it moves.

What this project taught me

Calm under pressure

Working through a complex model under pressure taught me to stay calm and take it one step at a time.

Attention to detail

In a 3D model, small details decide whether parts fit and move. The project trained me to check each one.

Reading engineering specs

I learnt to read engineering specifications and understand what each one means for how the product works.

Seeing the buyer’s benefit

I learnt to see the possibilities and benefits a hardware product brings to the people who use it, not only how it is built.

From spec to benefit

What the spec saysWhat it means for the user
4 degrees of freedomThe arm rotates and bends at several joints, so it can reach and position objects in more ways.
Gripper at the end of the armIt works directly with the environment, so one arm can grab items or carry a welding torch.
Stationary base and solid linksA stable base and rigid links give the arm a firm structure to move from.

This is the translation I do in product marketing: an engineering fact goes in, and a customer benefit comes out.

The parts and what they do

Joints (axes)

They allow movement such as rotation or bending between the links.
